_name: probe-2026-09-23-followups-to-cc - every follow-up on Container-CC, working from the previous turn's artifacts
_why:
Proves the feat/followups-to-cc branch on a rebuilt box (app AND cc-agent: the router prompt and the agent's CLAUDE.md both changed). Each case opens with an NExtSEEK graph question and follows up so that Container-CC must use what the previous turn left: its rows file, its Search details, its downloads, or its number. Route is asserted on every turn (seeds nextseek_query, follow-ups container_cc with a source of baml, followup or sticky), numbers are pinned by _measure, and reuse is asserted on cc_trace_text, the harness's view of the CC turn's tool calls (Read paths and Bash commands from the query_complete cc_traces).
  manage.py nessie --tier full --cases /app/NessieAI/tests/nessie_tests/probes/probe-2026-09-23-followups-to-cc.json --out /app/runs/followups-<date>
Every follow-up is a Container-CC turn and so the expensive kind: 10 CC turns and 11 NS turns in 10 cases.
_instance_warning:
EVERY NUMBER HERE WAS MEASURED ON THE WORKSTATION'S GRAPH ON 2026-09-23. Re-pin before the run:
  python NessieAI/tests/nessie_tests/scripts/pin_probe_truths.py --emit-cypher <this file>
  python ... pin_probe_truths.py --pin <this file> --from measured.json
Every case is mode 'each': list the numbers in the order of its locals.
_observability: What the harness sees of a CC turn: route and route_source (route_decided), the reply, the published artifacts and raw files (query_complete), and since this branch cc_trace_text, one line per tool call of the trace. The trace is conversation-scoped, so on a chat's SECOND CC turn it also holds the first CC turn's calls; every negative trace assertion here sits on a chat's first CC turn. The harness cannot see the staged /data/previous_turns tree itself, only the agent reading it.

followups_to_cc.description: Multi-turn: an NS graph seed, then follow-ups Container-CC must answer from that turn's artifacts.

variants.name: Analyse the previous rows: the species among those 73
variants._why: The seed's rows file holds every NHP it returned with its Species column (the operator's example turn: 73 NHP with flow AND sequencing data). The follow-up must be answered from that file: read under /data/previous_turns and no nextseek-query/parse/entity call rebuilding the result. Three species spellings, 47 + 22 + 4 = 73, measured 2026-09-23 on the workstation graph.

variants.name: Re-run the stored cypher with one change
variants._why: 'Same search but only D.SEQ': CC must take the Cypher from search_details.json and hand it to nextseek-graph with the flow requirement dropped. 351 NHP have sequencing data derived from them, against 73 with both. A reply of 73 means the change was not applied; any other number means the search was rebuilt rather than modified.

variants.name: Work with the downloaded file of the previous search
variants._why: 1,549 NDMA-treated mice fit under the 5,000-row cap, so the seed's graph_result_bundle file holds them all. 727 have Sex 'F' (820 'M', one 'F?', one 'DAM'); a reply of 728 counted the 'F?' too and is a judgement call, not a failure of reuse, so only 727 is pinned. If the seed's rows carry no Sex column CC may query the graph, which is allowed; rebuilding the seed with nextseek-query is not.

variants._why: 3,589 SRP mice (under the row cap). Genotype groups: 1,111, 626, 508, then the missing-value bucket (355), then 218 and 211. Whether the missing bucket counts as a 'group' is a reading of the question, so only the four numbers both readings share are pinned. Either the rows file or nextseek-aggregate is a correct path (the seed may not return Genotype); a rebuilt search is not.
